title: Levers as simple machines
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 6 Science and Technology; not yet checked by a CBC Science and Technology teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: A ruler on a pencil as a see-saw with coins, a bottle opener, a wheelbarrow, a jembe, a pair of tongs and a broom. The child marks the fulcrum (F), the effort (E) and the load (L) on each real tool before naming the class by what is in the middle.

skills.key_step: The child identifies a lever as a rigid bar that turns about a fixed point to move a load, and names levers in daily life (see-saw, wheelbarrow, bottle opener, jembe, broom, tongs).

floor.question: Is lifting a box a push or a pull?

representations: a ruler on a pencil with coins
a chart: tool, lever or not
steps: Find the point it turns on.
If all three are there, it is a lever.
contexts: a wheelbarrow on a building site

board.do: Draw a see-saw, a bucket and a bottle opener.

board.say: Does it turn on a fixed point to move a load?

board.do: Wait for the child to decide.
Write "lever" under the see-saw and the opener.

misconceptions.ask: Does a ladder turn on a point to lift a load?
misconceptions.repair: A ladder is not a lever.

misconceptions.ask: Is a bottle opener a lever?
Do you still do the work?
misconceptions.repair: A lever makes work easier; it gives no extra energy.

misconceptions.ask: Does the bucket turn on a fixed point?
misconceptions.repair: A handle alone does not make a lever.

checks.question: Give two levers used at home.
checks.answer: any two: bottle opener, broom, tongs, scissors, jembe

skills.key_step: The child marks the fulcrum (the turning point), the effort (where force is applied) and the load (what is moved) on a real lever, wherever they are.
representations: tools marked with F, E and L stickers
a drawing of a see-saw with labels
steps: Find where you push or pull: E.
contexts: a bottle opener on a soda top

board.say: Is this the fulcrum, the effort or the load?

board.do: Ask the child to mark E and L.

misconceptions.repair: Effort is your push; load is what is moved.
The fulcrum is the turning point.

misconceptions.ask: Does the wheel go up with the load?
misconceptions.repair: The fulcrum stays fixed while the lever turns.

listen_for: the fulcrum is in the middle
misconceptions.ask: What does the wheelbarrow turn on?
misconceptions.repair: The fulcrum can be at the end.

checks.question: Where is the fulcrum of a bottle opener?
checks.answer: the edge that rests on top of the bottle top

checks.question: What is the load when using tongs to lift charcoal?

skills.key_step: The child explains a lever makes work easier: less effort is needed when the effort is far from the fulcrum and the load is near it, and the work done is not reduced.

floor.prerequisite: Can mark the fulcrum, effort and load.
floor.question: What is the turning point of a lever called?

representations: a long and a short bar to lift a box
a ruler see-saw with coins at different places
steps: Keep the load and fulcrum fixed.
Move the effort further from the fulcrum.
Move the load closer to the fulcrum: easier too.
contexts: lifting a heavy stone with a bar
opening a paint tin with a spoon
carrying a load in a wheelbarrow

board.do: Draw a bar on a stone with a box at one end.
Ask where to push to lift the box most easily.
Draw a hand at the far end and write "far from the fulcrum: less effort".

listen_for: put the fulcrum near my hands
misconceptions.ask: Was it easier with the fulcrum near the load or near your hands?
misconceptions.repair: Fulcrum near the load means less effort.

misconceptions.ask: Where did you push to lift it easily?

misconceptions.repair: The load is the same; less effort, longer push.

misconceptions.ask: Which bar lifted the box with less effort?
misconceptions.repair: A longer bar needs less effort.

checks.question: To lift a heavy load with a bar, where should the effort be?
Does a lever make the load lighter?
checks.answer: No: it makes the effort smaller

skills.key_step: The child classifies a lever by the part in the middle: fulcrum in the middle (first class), load in the middle (second class), effort in the middle (third class).

floor.prerequisite: Can mark the fulcrum, effort and load.
floor.question: Where is the fulcrum of a see-saw?

representations: a "FLE 123" memory line: F middle 1st, L middle 2nd, E middle 3rd
steps: Mark F, E and L on the tool.
Find which one is in the middle.
F middle: first. L middle: second. E middle: third.

board.do: Draw tongs and mark F at the hinge.
Point at where the fingers squeeze.
board.say: Is this E or L, and is it in the middle?

misconceptions.ask: What is in the middle of a wheelbarrow?
misconceptions.repair: The middle part decides the class.

listen_for: it is big so it is first class
misconceptions.ask: Which part is in the middle?
misconceptions.repair: Class depends on the middle part, not size or use.

misconceptions.ask: Is the load or the effort in the middle of tongs?
misconceptions.repair: Load in the middle: second. Effort in the middle: third.

misconceptions.ask: Where is the pivot of the scissors?
misconceptions.repair: Fulcrum in the middle: first class.

checks.question: In which class is a wheelbarrow?
A lever has the effort in the middle. Which class is it?
